screens.name: Home
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a dominant orb, separate prompt and unavailable omen; supplied browser checks support proportional stability (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Give the unavailable omen a clearer recovery path while retaining the restrained hero composition.

screens.name: Approach
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves orb and caption placement between transition and settled captures, and supplied evidence describes automatic progression after 650ms (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Verify that automatic progression and its announcement remain understandable with assistive technology.

screens.name: Ask — normal
screens.evidence: Sheets 01–02 show the labeled question field, alternate voice action and clear submit button, with actual submission reported in the real drive (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Simplify the field’s doubled border treatment and replace technical prediction-engine wording with a plain explanation of how answers are used.

screens.name: Ask — 200% text and constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 01 and 14 show enlarged text and reachable submission, but the constrained capture shows only the tail of the question; supplied synthetic viewport checks report reachability (provisional A 7.0, F 6.7, overall 6.8).
findings: Verify native keyboard scrolling keeps the active question, caret and submit action available without forcing users to reconstruct hidden context.

screens.name: Listening — microphone failure
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows consistent entry and settled layouts with a microphone failure notice, Start listening and Type instead, while hardware speech remains unverified (provisional A 7.3, F 7.3, overall 7.3).
findings: After microphone failure, make the retry state explicit so “Speak your question” does not suggest recording is already active.

screens.name: Planning — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show a stable loading composition with a concrete phase explanation, duration expectation, credit reassurance and Cancel (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Confirm loading announcements and cancellation focus behavior on a physical screen reader.

screens.name: Follow-up 1 — plan readiness
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows readable progress and consistent answer rows, but “Barely started,” “Halfway there” and “Nearly certain” mix progress with confidence (provisional A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4).
findings: Validate that generated choices answer one consistent question dimension before treating this fixture layout as proof of semantic clarity.

screens.name: Follow-up 2 — obstacles
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show the same prompt-and-row structure through entry and settlement, with progress advancing to 2 of 3 (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Capture the selected standard answer and its advance feedback to establish continuity beyond the unselected rows.

screens.name: Follow-up 3 — support
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 shows a readable final question and 3-of-3 indicator, with actual follow-up completion reported separately (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Make the final choice’s immediate next step clear and verify that its transition announces the start of prediction generation.

screens.name: Custom answer — selected and empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows a checked custom choice, change-answer action, labeled empty field and disabled Continue in both entry and settled states (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Add a brief visible requirement near the field so the disabled Continue state explains what enables it.

screens.name: Custom answer — 200% empty, filled and constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 03 and 05 show substantial vertical expansion and horizontally clipped filled text, while supplied synthetic checks report retained answers and reachable submission (provisional A 6.7, F 7.0, overall 6.9).
findings: Use a wrapping answer field at enlarged text and reduce the selected-choice block so users can review their answer with its question.

screens.name: Research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 retains the planning layout while changing the phase explanation to research, with real HTTP completion reported in the supplied evidence (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Expose the phase change to assistive technology without repeatedly announcing the decorative animation.

screens.name: Reveal — collapsed
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show a subdued mid-entry headline becoming readable at rest, with forecast, uncertainty, date and multiple follow-up actions (provisional A 7.7, F 7.3, overall 7.5).
findings: Reduce competition among the lower actions and present the check-back date in a more readily scanned human format.

screens.name: Reveal — expanded explanation
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows an explicit collapse action and separated explanation, but its synthetic long-form content continues below the viewport (provisional A 7.0, F 7.3, overall 7.2).
findings: Structure long explanations into short labeled sections so reasons remain scannable without relying on a continuous paragraph.

screens.name: Check-in — outcome selection
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 places Yes, Not quite and Not yet beside the forecast context, and supplied runtime evidence reports saved and persisted outcomes (provisional A 7.7, F 7.3, overall 7.5).
findings: Distinguish outcome choices more clearly from text links and show the saved selection directly in the check-in view.

screens.name: Share
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows an orderly preview and format choices, while only PNG export and synthetic export-failure recovery are established by the supplied runtime account (provisional A 7.7, F 7.0, overall 7.3).
findings: Explain the friend link’s audience and access rules before presenting it as private.

screens.name: Story export
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows the bordered story composition and export action, with actual 1080×1920 PNG creation reported separately (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Increase the exported card’s smallest disclaimer text and verify legibility at typical social-feed display sizes.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows a stable empty state with a direct Ask the Ball action and a clear device-storage statement (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Give the empty-state action a stronger button affordance while preserving the open composition.

screens.name: History — populated and stress list
screens.evidence: Sheets 06–07 show dated rows and a long list extending behind fixed navigation, with history persistence reported in the real drive (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Make row activation clearer and verify the final row scrolls fully above the raised Ask orb and tab bar.

screens.name: Sky — offline sample stars
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 clearly label offline samples and the selected question, with a visible Retry and Ask this too action (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Give the selected star a non-color marker and verify each constellation label has a sufficiently large activation area.

screens.name: Circles — offline
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 announces offline availability before disabled creation and sharing controls, while the supplied evidence explicitly excludes a working social backend (provisional A 7.7, F 7.3, overall 7.5).
findings: State beside each disabled control whether connectivity or age eligibility is preventing its use.

screens.name: You — empty memory and settings
screens.evidence: Sheets 13 and 15 show consistent memory and preference sections, and supplied browser evidence establishes switch focus, keyboard activation and persistence (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Ensure the Privacy and entertainment row can rest fully above the raised navigation orb instead of appearing partially covered.

screens.name: You — 200% settings
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 shows enlarged settings with intact switches but clipped preceding content under the header and a lower action approaching fixed navigation (provisional A 7.3, F 7.7, overall 7.5).
findings: Verify enlarged rows can scroll into an unobscured reading position between the fixed header and navigation.

screens.name: Plans — normal
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 shows explicit billing units, yearly selection and simulation labels, but the settled capture cuts the decorative orb at the header (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Remove or fully reveal the small decorative orb so the settled plan view does not resemble a partially scrolled transition.

screens.name: Plans — 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 shows stacked prices, readable billing terms and a fully visible enlarged simulation action, with real payment behavior explicitly unverified (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify that pack alternatives and remaining plan details stay discoverable below the enlarged subscription action.

screens.name: Planning failure
screens.evidence: Sheets 05–06 show stable error hierarchy, credit reassurance, prominent retry and an edit-question escape route using explicitly labeled fixture content (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify retry preserves the question and announces the renewed loading state without losing focus.

screens.name: Prediction failure
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 adds Review answers to the failure recovery hierarchy while keeping retry primary and credit reassurance visible (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify recovery preserves all answers and returns users to the relevant context when they choose Review answers.

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — planning
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–12 show support, alternate-question and editing routes with an explicit no-credit/no-memory consequence, and a real redirect is reported separately (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Give the support route stronger prominence when support is the stated reason for declining the question.

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — prediction
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 preserves the redirect hierarchy across entry and settlement despite a more prominent mist frame (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Keep the support action visually primary and confirm the later redirect communicates what happened to previously entered answers.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: The orb consistently anchors the supplied screens, but acts as an invitation on Home and decoration elsewhere without screenshot proof of its semantics (provisional A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4).
findings: Give the interactive Home orb an explicit accessible name and keep decorative instances out of the accessibility tree.

components.name: Bottom tab bar
components.evidence: Sheets 07–08 and 13–15 show labeled tabs, gold active indicators and a raised central orb that overlaps nearby content (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Reserve bottom clearance for the protruding orb and verify enlarged labels and selected-tab announcements.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: The compact header remains consistent across sheets, and supplied runtime evidence reports correct balance after simulated purchases (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Distinguish daily allowance from purchased credits wherever “left today” could obscure the available balance.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream buttons provide consistent emphasis across normal and enlarged states, and supplied runtime checks establish several successful actions and disabled custom submission (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify focus, pressed and busy states consistently across every primary action rather than extrapolating from successful clicks.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text and underlined rows serve secondary actions throughout the sheets, with dense clusters beneath Reveal and some low-prominence support actions (provisional A 7.7, F 7.0, overall 7.3).
findings: Use a consistent secondary-action treatment and simplify clusters where several equally weighted links compete.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 02–04 show spacious underlined rows and a checked custom selection, but do not show a settled selected standard choice (provisional A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4).
findings: Demonstrate standard-choice selection feedback and expose selected state independently of color.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Sheets 01–02 show a persistent label, readable multiline value and strong field boundary, with actual input completion reported separately (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Remove the redundant inner line while preserving a distinct, clearly visible focus state.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Sheets 05 and 14 show clipped field content in enlarged constrained layouts despite reported answer retention and reachable submit actions (provisional A 6.7, F 6.7, overall 6.7).
findings: Wrap enlarged custom answers and verify caret visibility, full-value review and keyboard-safe scrolling on a physical phone.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 12–15 show labeled on/off states, and supplied control proof reports 342×52px rows, keyboard activation, visible focus and reload persistence (provisional A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0).
findings: Complete physical screen-reader and native text-enlargement checks before certifying these controls beyond browser behavior.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a compact unavailable omen with “Try again tomorrow,” but no populated omen or immediate recovery action is represented (provisional A 7.7, F 6.7, overall 7.1).
findings: Explain whether the absence is expected or temporary and provide an appropriate retry or fallback state.

components.name: Sky tabs
components.evidence: Sheets 05 and 13–14 distinguish Tonight’s Sky and Circles using text, gold color and an underline (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify tab roles, keyboard navigation and selected-state announcements.

components.name: Sky star and selected question
components.evidence: Sheets 13–14 connect a gold Love star to a labeled sample question and clear reuse button, but show no alternate selection or focus state (provisional A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4).
findings: Add a non-color selected marker and verify generous targets around the small stars.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheet 05 clearly separates offline status, invitation explanation and disabled controls, with backend availability explicitly excluded from the evidence (provisional A 7.7, F 7.3, overall 7.5).
findings: Consolidate repeated introductory copy and place each disabling reason beside the affected control.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 06–07 establish date, original question, forecast and status roles, while supplied evidence reports persistence and saved outcomes (provisional A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6).
findings: Clarify that the row opens a reading and make its status specific enough to distinguish waiting from an overdue check-in.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheet 09 shows a checked yearly option, explicit billing periods and stacked enlarged prices, with simulated purchase behavior reported separately (provisional A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8).
findings: Verify radio-group semantics and selection changes before treating the visible checkmark as accessible selection proof.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show a coherent export composition whose disclaimer and branding text become very small in the embedded preview (provisional A 7.3, F 6.5, overall 6.8).
findings: Increase the smallest card text and offer an accessible text equivalent for the image’s forecast and qualification.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Sheets 05–06, 08 and 12 show explicit failure, offline and redirect states with recovery routes, while supplied evidence reports recovery exercises (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Verify announcement timing and focus placement so errors are encountered immediately without displacing the recovery action.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently separate serif prompts from sans-serif controls, but metadata and exported qualifications are small and enlarged custom entry becomes cumbersome (provisional A 7.7, F 7.5, overall 7.6).
findings: Strengthen small metadata and tune enlarged input typography independently from decorative headline sizing.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The borderless mist remains coherent across the sheets, although brighter reveal and redirect frames pass behind content and final-candidate motion evidence is not unambiguous (provisional A 7.5, F 7.0, overall 7.2).
findings: Constrain mist luminance behind text and complete final-candidate motion and reduced-motion verification.

components.name: Progress indicator
components.evidence: Sheets 02–05 pair segmented progress with explicit step counts at normal and enlarged sizes (provisional A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7).
findings: Announce step changes with the new question and preserve the explicit count for users who cannot distinguish segment colors.

limitations: All grades are provisional; supplied runtime results were considered as reported evidence and were not independently replayed.
A is the normalized mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the normalized mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall uses 0.4A + 0.6F before rounding.
Null denotes only genuinely inapplicable dimensions; absent interaction or accessibility evidence instead lowers confidence in numeric scores.
The 17 core states and their represented variants are covered above, with each transition assessed alongside its corresponding settled state.
Static transition pairs establish visual correspondence, not uninterrupted motion, timing, focus continuity or freedom from intermediate contrast loss.

The supplied narrative reports a candidate motion pass, then describes later enlarged-form changes with a current trace still being repeated; a final-build motion pass cannot be established unambiguously.
Synthetic layout predictions and repeated explanation text establish layout stress only, not model quality, relevance or predictive accuracy.
Physical iPhone behavior, native Dynamic Type, real keyboards, VoiceOver/TalkBack, microphone hardware, haptics, real payments, social backend and OS sharing remain unverified.

Synthetic keyboard captures show clipping and reduced context, but supplied reachability checks prevent concluding that the primary action is inaccessible; no hard-gate failure is conclusively established.

Populated memory editing, reminder confirmation, saved outcome styling, alternate standard-choice selection and export-failure presentation lack corresponding screenshots despite some reported runtime coverage.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met; the evidence also does not permit 9/10 certification.
topFixes: Fix enlarged custom-answer readability with wrapping text and preserved question context; verify on a physical keyboard.
Ensure content can scroll fully clear of fixed headers, navigation and the raised Ask orb.
Improve small metadata and share-card qualifications, and constrain mist brightness behind text.
Clarify microphone retry, disabled controls, outcome selection and private-link access.
Complete final-candidate transition, physical-device and assistive-technology evidence before seeking premium certification.
